intro: 上 is literally 'top' or 'on'. As a grammar word it keeps that spatial image: 上で stands on one action as a foundation for the next step, and 上に piles one fact on top of another. Ask whether the first clause is a base you stand on (上で) or a layer you add to (上に).

skills.rule: V-た上で: only after first doing X (as a prerequisite), do Y; V-る上で: in doing X, or for the purpose of X, something is important or necessary.
skills.explain:
上で has two forms with two jobs. After the past form, V-た上で means 'after doing X, and on that basis': the first action is a deliberate prerequisite for a decision or action that follows. よく考えた上で決めます. With a suru-noun you can also say Nの上で: 相談の上で, 確認の上 (formal notices often drop the で).

After the dictionary form, V-る上で means 'in doing X' or 'for X': the main clause says what matters, helps or needs care for that activity. Typical endings are 大切だ, 必要だ, 役に立つ, 注意する. 日本で生活する上で、言葉は大切だ. Nの上では also means 'in terms of N': 法律の上では問題ない.

The edge: V-た上で is not a plain 'and then'. Ordinary sequences take てから or て. The tense is the switch: た = after, る = in doing. And 上で never adds an extra fact; that is 上に.
patterns: [verb dictionary form] 上で、[大切 / 必要 / 注意する]

examples.jp: よく考[かんが]えた{上[うえ]で}決[き]めてください。
examples.en: Please decide after thinking it over carefully.

examples.jp: 家族[かぞく]と相談[そうだん]した{上[うえ]で}、お返事[へんじ]します。
examples.en: I'll give you my answer after talking it over with my family.

examples.jp: 詳[くわ]しいことは、話[はな]し合[あ]いの{上[うえ]で}決[き]めましょう。
examples.en: Let's decide the details after we have discussed them.

examples.jp: 外国語[がいこくご]を学[まな]ぶ{上[うえ]で}、一番[いちばん]大切[たいせつ]なのは毎日[まいにち]続[つづ]けることだ。
examples.en: In learning a foreign language, the most important thing is to keep at it every day.

examples.jp: この仕事[しごと]をする{上[うえ]で}、注意[ちゅうい]すべき点[てん]がいくつかあります。
examples.en: There are a few points to be careful about in doing this job.

examples.jp: 法律[ほうりつ]の{上[うえ]で}は、何[なに]も問題[もんだい]ありません。
examples.en: Legally speaking, there is no problem at all.

contrast.note: 上に adds a second fact on top of the first: 安い上においしい (cheap, and tasty as well). 上で sets a prerequisite or a purpose; it never means 'and also'.
てから is a neutral 'after'. V-た上で adds 'and having done that properly, on that basis'. 起きてから顔を洗う is a plain sequence; 起きた上で顔を洗う is wrong.
V-た上は means 'now that X has happened, I must': 引き受けた上は、最後までやる. It is a formal からには, followed by resolve or duty. V-た上で is followed by the action that the prerequisite makes possible.

mistakes.bad: 朝[あさ]起[お]きた{上[うえ]で}、歯[は]を磨[みが]きます。
mistakes.good: 朝[あさ]起[お]きて{から}、歯[は]を磨[みが]きます。
mistakes.note: A routine sequence is not a deliberate prerequisite; use てから.

mistakes.bad: 日本[にほん]で生活[せいかつ]した{上[うえ]で}、大切[たいせつ]なことは何[なん]ですか。
mistakes.good: 日本[にほん]で生活[せいかつ]する{上[うえ]で}、大切[たいせつ]なことは何[なん]ですか。
mistakes.note: 'In doing X, what matters' takes the dictionary form: する上で.

mistakes.bad: この店[みせ]は安[やす]い{上[うえ]で}、おいしい。
mistakes.good: この店[みせ]は安[やす]い{上[うえ]に}、おいしい。
mistakes.note: Adding a second good point is 上に, not 上で.

skills.tip: Look at the verb before 上で: た means 'first do it, then act on it'; る means 'for doing it, this matters'.

skills.rule: X 上に Y: X is true, and on top of that Y is true as well, with both facts pointing the same way.
skills.explain:
上に stacks facts: 'not only X, but also Y'. Both facts push in the same direction, both good or both bad: 広い上に駅から近い, 道に迷った上に雨まで降ってきた. Y is often marked with も or まで to show it is the extra layer.

It joins to the plain form: verbs (遅れた上に), i-adjectives (寒い上に), na-adjectives with な (親切な上に), nouns with の or である (医者である上に).

Two limits. First, the main clause states a fact; it cannot be a command, request, invitation or statement of intention. 安い上に、ぜひ買ってください is wrong; use から. Second, the two facts must not pull against each other: for 'expensive but tasty' use けど or のに, not 上に.
patterns: [plain verb / i-adjective] 上に、[noun] も [more of the same]

examples.jp: この部屋[へや]は広[ひろ]い{上[うえ]に}、駅[えき]からも近[ちか]い。
examples.en: This flat is spacious, and it's close to the station too.

examples.jp: 今日[きょう]は寒[さむ]い{上[うえ]に}、風[かぜ]も強[つよ]い。
examples.en: It's cold today, and on top of that the wind is strong.

examples.jp: 田中[たなか]さんは親切[しんせつ]な{上[うえ]に}、仕事[しごと]もよくできる。
examples.en: Tanaka-san is kind, and good at the job as well.

examples.jp: 昨日[きのう]は寝坊[ねぼう]した{上[うえ]に}、財布[さいふ]まで忘[わす]れてしまった。
examples.en: Yesterday I overslept, and on top of that I even forgot my wallet.

examples.jp: 彼女[かのじょ]は医者[いしゃ]である{上[うえ]に}、小説[しょうせつ]も書[か]いている。
examples.en: She is a doctor, and she writes novels as well.

examples.jp: ごちそうになった{上[うえ]に}、お土産[みやげ]までいただきました。
examples.en: Not only did they treat me to a meal, they even gave me a present.

contrast.note: 上で means 'after doing' (V-た上で) or 'in doing' (V-る上で). It never adds a second fact. If you can say 'and what's more', it is 上に.
ばかりか is a stronger 'not only... but even', usually with も or まで and often a surprising second fact. 上に is a calmer 'besides'. Both add; ばかりか leans on the surprise.
くせに means 'even though', with criticism: 知っているくせに教えない. It sets up a clash; 上に piles up facts in agreement.

mistakes.bad: この店[みせ]は高[たか]い{上[うえ]に}、おいしい。
mistakes.good: この店[みせ]は高[たか]い{けど}、おいしい。
mistakes.note: Expensive (bad) and tasty (good) pull in opposite directions, so 上に cannot join them.

mistakes.bad: このパソコンは軽[かる]い{上[うえ]に}、ぜひ使[つか]ってみてください。
mistakes.good: このパソコンは軽[かる]い{から}、ぜひ使[つか]ってみてください。
mistakes.note: 上に cannot be followed by a request or command.

mistakes.bad: 彼[かれ]は親切[しんせつ]{上[うえ]に}、頭[あたま]もいい。
mistakes.good: 彼[かれ]は親切[しんせつ]な{上[うえ]に}、頭[あたま]もいい。
mistakes.note: A na-adjective needs な before 上に.

skills.tip: Can you insert 'and what's more' between the clauses, with both facts on the same side? Then it is 上に.
